primary_meaning: The righteous person who flourishes uprightly and fruitfully under God's blessing
primary_basis: Jeremiah 17:7-8 (parallel imagery of the thriving tree)
Temple and tabernacle decorations featuring palms (1 Kings 6–7; Ezekiel 40–41) as signs of life and blessing

alternatives.meaning: Victory, triumph, and festive acclamation (especially via palm branches)
basis: 1 Maccabees 13:51; 2 Maccabees 10:7 (intertestamental background often noted in Christian commentaries)

alternatives.meaning: Rest, refreshment, and divine provision in the wilderness
Place of judgment, leadership, or sacred association (via named palms)
basis: Deuteronomy 34:3; 2 Chronicles 28:15 (Jericho as city of palms)

notes: Christian teaching most consistently treats the palm tree itself (tamar) as an emblem of the flourishing righteous, drawing directly on Psalm 92; the closely related palm-branch motif of victory is extremely common but technically distinct and centered on the fronds rather than the tree. No major confessional tradition assigns a contradictory primary sense.
